events.title: Tropical precarity
events.summary: Explore the intersections of performance, visual art, gender expression, and cultural resistance in Puerto Rico through a conversation with acclaimed artists Freddie Mercado Velázquez and Mickey Negrón. This event delves into queer aesthetics and cultural identity.

evidence.description: The Latina/o Studies and the Contemporary Performance in Puerto Rico Working Group, in partnership with the Department of American Culture, invites you to Tropical Precarity: Drag and Visual Arts in Puerto Rico, a special performance and panel discussion. This event features an in-depth conversation with acclaimed Puerto Rican artists Freddie Mercado Velázquez and Mickey Negrón, exploring the intersections of performance, visual art, gender expression, and cultural resistance.

events.summary: Explore the hidden environmental and human costs of artificial intelligence in this film screening. The event delves into the often-unseen labor and resource consumption behind AI technologies, offering a critical perspective on its development.

evidence.venue: Ann Arbor District Library Downtown, 343 S. Fifth Avenue, Ann Arbor
evidence.description:
Artificial Intelligence fuels our dreams and nightmares. But while tech giants promise the advent of a new humanity, behind the scenes AI remains totally hidden. While data centers concrete over landscapes and dry up rivers, millions of workers around the world prepare the billions of data that will feed Big Tech's voracious algorithms, at the cost of their mental and emotional health. They are hidden 'in the belly' of AI.

Join community members and friends of MCSP for this screening of a film that looks beyond the headline grabbing threats of AI to the environmental and human costs.
